title: Out & About with Barney: Indianapolis astrophysicist featured in new series highlighting science careers
excerpt: Discover the Apophis asteroid 2029 and its expected close approach to Earth. Learn from expert Dr. Jeremy Wood about this event.
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — A new series is bringing science to life by highlighting the people behind groundbreaking discoveries.

“Bright Minds – Cool Careers,” a segment on “Out & About with Barney,” hosted by Barney Wood, features Dr. Jeremy Wood, a theoretical astrophysicist who studies asteroids and explores the mysteries of space.

Dr. Jeremy Wood focuses on near-Earth objects, or NEOs, and helps NASA track them. One asteroid drawing attention is Apophis, which is expected to make a close approach to Earth in 2029.

“We’re keeping a close eye on Apophis,” Dr. Wood said. “It’s going to give us quite a show in 2029.”

The asteroid, which measures about 450 meters across, is expected to pass approximately 20,000 miles from Earth — closer than some satellites orbit the planet. It will be visible to the naked eye in parts of the world under favorable viewing conditions.

The encounter will provide scientists with an opportunity to study the asteroid during its close approach.

Dr. Wood has also contributed to the understanding of ring systems around small celestial bodies. His research helped establish what is known as the “Wood limit,” which describes the distance at which a body’s gravity influences the orbits of particles in a ring system.

“In 2013, we discovered that a small comet-like body had rings,” Dr. Wood said. “Everyone thought only planets could have rings. We proved them wrong.”

Dr. Wood’s interest in space began when he was 7 years old. His sister, Janie, gave him a book titled “What’s Up There,” which helped spark his fascination with astronomy.

“That book changed everything, “Barney said.

Growing up in a large Irish Catholic family, Dr. Wood never imagined he would meet his hero, William Shatner. He eventually met the actor, who called him onstage during a question-and-answer session.

Barney explained that space plays an important role in everyday life on Earth, from satellite communications and solar-related signal disruptions to the aurora borealis. He also noted that advances such as the James Webb Space Telescope and the study of exoplanets continue to expand our understanding of the universe.

“Bright Minds – Cool Careers” will continue highlighting scientists and professionals making a difference.
